paper-white.tonalNote: The Spectra 6 panel admits no tonal steps. Every ramp here is one step by construction; a lighter or darker variant would quantize back to one of the six inks or to noise.

ink-black.tonalNote: Structural color: rules, numerals, labels, route lines, footer inversion. No gray step exists.

alarm-red.tonalNote: The loudest report: overdue, down, urgent, dangerous heat or air, the critical/doorbell alert band.

caution-yellow.tonalNote: The middle report: due today, warn, stale, low battery, quota running out, the important alert band.

healthy-green.tonalNote: Confirms a clean/OK reading on a status mark. Never a title, never a percentage.

weather-blue.tonalNote: Rain, a calendar's own identity color, and the humidity trace on the desk chart.

hero.purpose: The weather page's own NOW temperature. At most one per page.

headline.purpose: A page's own dominant reading or statement: the header day numeral, the device battery percent, the alert title.

title.purpose: The numbers inside a field: AI capacity, uptime, header weather temperature, desk temperature and humidity.

body.purpose: Every reading row and running-text line: priorities, agenda, brief text, sensor and service names, the alert message.

label.purpose: The small caps caption beneath or beside every numeral and every field.

icon.purpose: Nerd Font glyphs, sized one to three px larger than the text they sit beside.

components.name: Numeral and Label Field
components.description: The panel's base grammar: a tabular numeral with its unit, and a small-caps label beneath it.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-start; gap: 4px; } .ds-numeral { font-family: 'Google Sans', sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: 48px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; color: #000000; } .ds-unit { font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700; margin-left: 2px; } .ds-label { font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: #000000; }

components.name: State Chip (red)
components.description: A borderless filled pill reporting an overdue or critical state on a row.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 2px 6px 3px; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.02em; text-transform: uppercase; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-chip-red { background: #FF0000; color: #FFFFFF; }

components.name: State Chip (yellow)
components.description: A borderless filled pill reporting a due-today or caution state on a row.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 2px 6px 3px; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.02em; text-transform: uppercase; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-chip-yellow { background: #FFFF00; color: #000000; }

components.name: Chip, plain
components.description: The unfilled default: a due date or caption with no state to report yet.
components.css: .ds-chip-plain { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.02em; color: #000000; white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Tell-tale
components.description: A small filled circle preceding a word or reading to flag a state without recoloring the reading itself.
components.css: .ds-row { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.04em; } .ds-telltale { display: inline-block; width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 50%; } .ds-telltale-red { background: #FF0000; }

components.name: Line Meter
components.description: A thin outlined bar filled from the left for a used fraction; empty means unknown, never a guess.
components.css: .ds-meter { position: relative; height: 4px; border: 2px solid #000000; background: #FFFFFF; box-sizing: content-box; } .ds-meter-fill { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; height: 100%; background: #000000; }

components.name: Hatch (unavailable)
components.description: A 45 degree black-and-white stripe box standing in for any value that is unknown or unavailable, in place of a numeral.

components.name: Window List (footer)
components.description: The five-page footer navigation, matching the device's physical left/right buttons; the current page inverts to a solid black block.
components.html: 1 TODAY2 AGENDA!3 WEATHER
components.css: .ds-winlist { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 24px; height: 40px; font-family: 'Google Sans', sans-serif; } .ds-win { font-size: 20px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #000000; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-win-active { background: #000000; color: #FFFFFF; height: 32px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 0 8px; }

narrative.overview:
deskmate is an instrument front panel rendered on paper. Every value the owner needs is a large numeral with its small capital label sitting beneath it; fields are split by a 2 px rule, not a boxed tile; one vertical scale is where time itself runs, on the agenda page's route. There is no title bar and no page-name band: the page's own name lives once, in the footer window list, so nothing on the page repeats what the footer already says.

The surface is unforgiving by construction and the system is built out of that. Every page is an exact 800x480 still, quantized to six pure colors with no dithering (tested on the physical panel and rejected), refreshed in about 32 seconds. There is no motion, no hover, no second state, no breakpoint. Weight and size are the only reliable hierarchy at these dimensions, so a numeral is drawn large and its label is drawn heavy rather than drawn small.

Color still reports state, not decoration, everywhere except one page: the alert page is itself a state, so its priority color is allowed to fill the top band the way nothing else on the panel is allowed to. Elsewhere a colored field is always news: a chip, a tell-tale dot, a meter fill, a route line. The explicit anti-reference remains the phone-widget look the owner named directly: rounded app cards, app-store gloss, generic dashboard tiles. Nothing here is rounded except the tell-tale and route dots, which are marks, never containers.
keyCharacteristics: Numeral over small-caps label is the base grammar of the whole panel.
2 px black rules divide fields; there is no boxed tile and no title bar.
Six pure colors, no dithering, no gray, no gradient, no shadow.
A color fills a field only to report a state, with one exception: the alert page's top band, which is the state.
Tell-tale dots and route/day dots are the panel's only round shapes.
Icons come only from the bundled Nerd Font subset.
Fixed 800x480 frame: nothing reflows, overflow clips or two-line clamps.

rules.name: The State-Or-Nothing Rule
rules.body: A field takes a color only at the instant it reports a state: red for overdue, down, urgent or dangerous heat/air; yellow for due today, warn, stale, or low; green for a confirmed-healthy reading; blue for rain or a calendar's identity. The one exception in the whole build is the alert page's top band, which is the state and is allowed to fill a whole region in its priority color.

rules.name: The Six-Colors-Exactly Rule
rules.body: Only the six panel colors may appear in a shipped raster (app/renderer/palette.py:assert_palette). No gray, no tint, no opacity, no gradient. A seventh color is a build failure, not a rounding error.

rules.name: The Quiet-Green Rule
rules.body: Green confirms; it never leads. It appears on a status mark or a tell-tale, never as a fill behind a percentage or a whole field.

rules.name: The Numeral-And-Label Rule
rules.body: Every value on the panel is a large numeral (or, on the alert page, a large statement) with its own small-caps label beneath or beside it. A page never shows a bare number without the label that says what it is.

rules.name: The Fourteen-Pixel Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the panel is drawn below 14 px, in HTML or in SVG; 16 px is the default label size and 14 px is reserved for the three places measured to need it, Brief's own due-chip type included.

rules.name: The Heavy-Label Rule
rules.body: Labels are set at 700 weight in uppercase; body and numeral type stay at 500 to 600. Weight, not size, is what survives quantization at the label's own small sizes.

rules.name: The 456 Rule
rules.body: Today, Agenda, Weather and Brief all give their left column exactly 456 px; whatever is left, minus the 2 px rule and its 16 px padding on each side, is the right column's own width.

rules.name: The No-Name-Band Rule
rules.body: A page's own name appears exactly once, in the footer window list. No page repeats it in a header band, a title bar or a kicker above its own content.

rules.name: The Clip-Never-Reflow Rule
rules.body: The page cannot get taller or scroll, so overflow is resolved by clipping, ellipsis or a two-line clamp, decided once in the view layer, never left to the template to discover at render time.

rules.name: The Flat-Paper Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat, always. The only emphasis available is a 2 px rule, a 2 px border, or full inversion to black.

dos: Do pair every numeral with its own small-caps label beneath or beside it (The Numeral-And-Label Rule).
Do split fields with a 2 px rule; never box a field in a bordered tile.
Do give Today, Agenda, Weather and Brief a 456 px left column (The 456 Rule).
Do spend color only to report a state, and remember the alert page's top band is the one field allowed to be colored for its own sake (The State-Or-Nothing Rule).
Do hold the 14 px floor, default to 16 px, and set label type at 700 weight (The Fourteen-Pixel Floor Rule, The Heavy-Label Rule).
Do draw an unknown or unavailable value as a hatch box, never as a guessed number.
Do name a page exactly once, in the footer window list (The No-Name-Band Rule).
Do decide truncation once in app/view.py and only clip or two-line clamp in the template (The Clip-Never-Reflow Rule).
donts: Don't introduce a seventh color, a gray, a tint, an opacity or a gradient (The Six-Colors-Exactly Rule).
Don't add a shadow, a lift, a frosted layer or any depth besides a rule, a 2 px border, or full inversion to black (The Flat-Paper Rule).
Don't fill a title bar or a whole field with green, or color a healthy percentage at all (The Quiet-Green Rule).
Don't put a boxed tile, a title bar, or a page-name band above a page's own content; the footer already carries the page's name.
Don't round a corner on a field, chip, meter or hatch box; the round shapes on this panel are marks (tell-tale and event dots) only.
Don't use a Unicode symbol, emoji, or plain text character as a stand-in for an icon the bundled Nerd Font subset does not contain.
Don't write hover, focus, transition, animation or a media query; the panel has one state and one size.
